objective: 0.3.0 pi 7/10: Implement the specialist launcher and workflow tool for Pi, so the root dispatches Assignments to Pi child processes and receives their completion without blocking.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.

Maintainer, 2026-11-07: implement 0.3.0 now, every part except the dropped auto-mode gate (pi 8/10); test with unit tests and recorded or synthesized fixtures only, no live Kimi runs; merge each PR once it is reviewed and green.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.

The launcher is @tintinweb/pi-subagents (decided): it accepts only the eighteen specialist names, takes model and effort from the dispatched entry, is callable from codemode where the package allows it, and reports progress; HolyAgent adds launcher glue (a holy_assign tool or other code) only for a requirement the package does not meet, which is verified when the launcher is built.

Each child is started with --model <provider/id>:<thinking>, --tools or --exclude-tools from the role, --append-system-prompt with the role file, --session-id derived from the Assignment id (letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen, starting and ending alphanumeric), --session-dir and the HolyAgent extension through -e.

A launch is non-blocking: the root ends its turn and a completion notice starts a new root turn (pi.sendMessage with triggerTurn); the shipped subagent example blocks per child, so it is the source for flags only.
A warm specialist is continued through the same session id with a new prompt, only when the CLI's directive says continue; a specialist whose review must be independent is never continued.

Completion is read from agent_settled, never agent_end; failure from stopReason error, aborted or length, a failed auto_retry_end, a process exit or a settle without a report, each mapped to the Assignment status table of orchestration.md.

After a launch the launcher records the agent id with assignment record under the dispatched-Assignment marker test and says so in its tool result; on failure it hands the step back to the root. It keeps launched agent ids (pid, session id) where a resumed root can read them.

Decided (maintainer): no workflow script asks for confirmation, whatever agents it calls, consistent with full access as the default ("No confirmation"); the earlier ctx.ui.confirm gate for scripts that call agents other than the eighteen specialists is dropped.
When the package's workflow tool or codemode is not among the active tools, the launcher provides a direct subagent fallback and signals workflows-unavailable to the runtime switch.
Abort and deadlines are the host's job; the launcher sets PI_CACHE_RETENTION=long on children where the provider's adapter honors it.

Maintainer (verbatim): "for the kimi provider, currently kimi k3.1 pro should be root and the kimi-for-coding model (which is kimi k2.8 preview) should be the specialists, except stuff like visual stuff that should be kimi k3.1 pro low or something. it really depends on the specialists and the routing should be figured out".
The launcher picks each specialist's model and thinking level from the Kimi route table of Intent 0.3.0 pi 5/10 when Kimi for Coding is the configured provider.

Decided (maintainer): specialists and workflows run through @tintinweb/pi-subagents; its SubagentWorkflow tool runs Claude-style workflow scripts in the background, so the root stays free and is woken as each specialist finishes.
Decided: no extra report tool; a specialist's final message is its report.

Carried from the Kimi set review: the root and role prompt files built for Pi pass through stripCitations like the skills, and stripCitations handles the reviewed edge cases: a stray backtick pairing code spans across list items, a fence indented four or more spaces with a blank line inside, a final-line comment keeping the preceding newline, with tests; docs/development.md states that code spans and fenced blocks are left as written.
